mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1500, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, stimulating equity markets and yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, always.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators' impact on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in two consecutive months signals a supply chain disruption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, a high and rising GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong aggregate demand, which consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP and equity market correlation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is above 250, the combined monetary and inflationary pressure predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% in a quarter and CPIAUCSL > 250
regime_hint: monetary tightening cycle with high inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% without a corresponding increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) suggests labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

evidence_refs: fact:historical retail_sales and equity market correlation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
